item.title: Self-Hosted Confidential Computing: Gramine vs Occlum vs Enarx TEE Platforms
item.description: Confidential computing uses hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to protect data while it is being processed. Unlike encryption at rest and in transit, TEEs shield data in use — preventing even the host operating system, hypervisor, or cloud provider from accessing sensitive workloads. Three open-source platforms lead this space: Gramine, Occlum, and Enarx. Each takes a fundamentally different architectural approach to enabling confidential computing for self-hosted deployments.
